# Tools Used to Make This Book {#sec-appendixB}

To set up the environment for replicating the code used in this book the
R language is needed as well as R and Rstudio IDE environments. The
following sections contain the directions for installing **R** and
**RStudio**, how to set up a book with **quarto** and how to use
**GitHub** as a version saver source.

## RStudio installation

Download and install R and RStudio Desktop:
<https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>

## How to setup this project with quarto

[**Quarto**](https://quarto.org/) is the new version of
[**Rmarkdown**](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/), it can be used for
making notes, presentations, websites, books and more.

In this project the book has been made in quarto and version saved on
github.

For more information about how to publish a quarto book have a look
here: [Quarto
publishing](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html)

### GitHub useful commands

You can do the same using the command line. In RStudio create a new
project on a new directory, add git, and select `quarto book project`

The automated process will create a `_quarto.yml` file, the top of the
file will look like this one:

``` r
---
project:
        type: book
---
```

On terminal type: `quarto preview`, it will create a folder `_book`.

#### Add Github afterwords

[existing-github-last](https://happygitwithr.com/existing-github-last.html)
to connect with github create a github repo with the same name of your
project then type

``` r
usethis::use_git()
```

It asks you to commit all files in the RStudio project. This pushes all
files in R to a remote folder designed to head to the github repo.

In terminal connect with the github repo:

``` r
# on terminal type

git init 
git remote add origin
```

https://github.com/Fgazzelloni/infectious.git

``` r
# on terminal type

git branch -M main 
git push -u origin main 
```

### Publish your book on github pages

change the `quarto.yml` file into:

``` r
---
project: 
  type: book 
  output-dir: docs 
---
```

add a .nojekyll file, type in terminal:

``` r
# on terminal type

touch .nojekyll 
```

then type

``` r
# on terminal type

quarto render 
```

some issues might arise if more than one calculation is made inside a
single chunks split the chunks!

quarto render creates a folder `docs`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Add a package

``` r
devtools::create("yourpkg")
```

Now that you have your book done, you might need to add some customized
data to use within your analysis.

In order to do that, you'll need to just add data in the way that is
usually done when inside a package.

### Building blocks of the R package inside the quarto book

#### Add data to the package

set the data from the original source and tidy appropriately

``` r
usethis::use_data_raw()
```

it creates a .R script where to put the steps for get the data ready

once data are ready

``` r
usethis::use_data(yourdata)
```

It creates the R folder where the .R scripts of data documentation is
located

``` r
usethis::use_r("yourdataset")
```

read how to document your work

``` r
vignette("rd-other") # for datasets
vignette("rd")

devtools::document()
devtools::load_all(".")
```

#### Add package information

so the ? (NAMESPACE) works

``` r
usethis::use_package_doc()
devtools::document()
```

#### Add data information

``` r
usethis::use_r("yourdataset")
devtools::document()
```

when filling the data .R script for explaining what's inside the dataset
a specific structure needs to be used (see examples)

when new data are added

Build tab and ---\> More ---\> clean and install (this is not there
anymore when you start with `devtools::create("yourpkg")`) to add the
new data to NAMESPACE
